hyps.why: With edge 0 absent, edge 3 is often the main input-to-output path, so removing it can disconnect the cell and collapse accuracy.
Without edge 4, removing edge 5 cuts off the paths to the output node and gives near-chance accuracy.
When edge 3 is none, edge 5 carries a needed route to the output, so removing it is far more damaging.
Replacing a parameter-free pool on the first edge with a 3x3 convolution adds a lot of capacity, as in the huge gains seen from pool and skip parents.
Swapping a pool for a 3x3 convolution on the direct edge gives larger gains than replacing ops that already have parameters.
Adding a convolution on a missing edge 4 restores a path and was consistently positive across experiments.
Reviving an absent direct edge with a convolution adds capacity and connectivity, giving a large positive effect.
Filling an empty edge 1 with a 3x3 convolution adds a useful path, unlike replacing an existing op.
Restoring a missing final edge with a convolution reconnects the output and improves accuracy more than modifying an existing op.
Deleting an existing 1x1 convolution on edge 4 loses real capacity and was clearly harmful, unlike removing a pool, which can help.
